# Mendix Project: erpv1

Built with mxcli and MDL (Mendix Definition Language).

## Project Brain — read this first

If `docs/brain/` exists, read `docs/brain/project.md` before doing anything
else. It holds the decisions this project has already made — things no command can
tell you, and that are cheap to contradict by accident.

Then, depending on what you are doing:

- **Building in a module** — also read `docs/brain/modules/<Module>.md` for the
  modules you are about to touch. Not the whole directory; only those.
- **Working a slice** — `./mxcli brain brief --slice <name> -p project.mpr` emits
  exactly that pack (project + the slice's modules + its plan) as one read.
- **Planning, or picking work up** — run `./mxcli brain plan -p project.mpr`.
  It reports what is built from the model itself, so it cannot be out of date.

Record what you learn with `./mxcli brain capture`. Read
`.ai-context/skills/project-brain/SKILL.md` for what belongs there and what does not —
the short version is that anything mxcli can answer must never be written down.

## Communication Style

- **Never show raw MDL in chat.** Describe changes in plain language as a numbered list.
- Unless exec approval resolves to `ask` (`bin/exec-approval.sh <project-root>`), write the MDL to a script file, validate it, execute it through `bin/exec.sh`, and report what ran — no approval round-trip.
- Show MDL only if the user asks to see the script.
- Report results as plain language, not as a diff.

## Running mxcli

The binary is in the **root of this project**, not on `PATH` — always `./mxcli`.

```bash
./mxcli -p project.mpr -c "DESCRIBE STRUCTURE"   # one command
./mxcli exec script.mdl -p project.mpr        # a script
```

Scripts live in `mdlsource/`, one file per concern.
**Each starts with `mdl 1;`.** A headerless one is `mdl 0`: upgrade it first,
`./mxcli fmt --upgrade --header -p project.mpr -w <file>`, then
`check --deprecations=error --v1=error` it; never mix them in a file.
Exec a change twice: the second run must write nothing (unchanged).

## The gates, in order

Run them cheapest-first; each is only worth paying for once the one above is clean.
**They are the definition of done, not a menu** — a change is finished when they have
all been run and you have said what each one reported.

**Once per change, not per edit** — a change being a coherent unit of work, not a
statement and not a file write. Iterate with `exec`, then run the gates once over the
result: the whole list after every edit proves nothing the one run at the end does not.

```bash
./mxcli check script.mdl -p project.mpr      # syntax + references, no apply (~2s)
./mxcli exec script.mdl -p project.mpr       # apply
./mxcli lint -p project.mpr                  # rules (~3s)
./mxcli report -p project.mpr                # scored quality report
./mxcli docker check -p project.mpr          # mxbuild, the slow one (~25s)
./mxcli test tests/ -p project.mpr --local   # microflow tests (~30s cold, ~2s warm)
./mxcli run --local --watch --detach -p project.mpr   # the app, backgrounded; then `run wait`/`status`/`stop`
```

**`lint` printing no errors is not a pass** — read the warning count, and read
`report`'s score. A green `check` proves nothing about behaviour or about how
a page renders: logic needs `test`, and anything visual needs the app actually running.

Set `mx` up once with `./mxcli setup mxbuild -p project.mpr`. To call it directly,
name the version — `~/.mxcli/mxbuild/<version>/modeler/mx` — because a `*` glob
breaks the moment two are cached.

## Syntax, rules and skills — ask the tool, not this file

These change every release, and a copy that disagrees with the tool is worse than none.

| To find out | Run |
|---|---|
| How to write any MDL — **before any skill** | `./mxcli syntax` → `./mxcli syntax <topic> [sub]` |
| Which lint rules exist | `./mxcli lint -p project.mpr --list-rules` |
| What a command takes | `./mxcli help <command>` |
| What this project contains | `./mxcli -p project.mpr -c "DESCRIBE STRUCTURE"` |
| Why it was built this way | `docs/brain/` (above) |

**Skills** are in `.ai-context/skills/<name>/SKILL.md` (and `.claude/skills/`, which is
the path Claude Code scans). Each one's frontmatter `description` says when to reach for
it — that IS the index, so list the directory rather than looking for a table.

**Read a skill's section, not the file** — each opens with a line-numbered index.

## Conventions no command will tell you

- **Quote every identifier** in MDL — `Module."Customer"`, `"Status": String(50)`.
  Quotes are stripped, so it is safe and sidesteps every parser keyword.
  It does **not** exempt names Mendix itself reserves (`Type`, `ID`, `CreatedDate`) —
  those are rejected quoted or not.
- **A business process with human steps is a `WORKFLOW`**, not a status attribute
  plus microflows — you get the user-task inbox, assignment, timers and a definition
  the business can read. `mxcli syntax workflow`, skill `write-workflows`.
- **An aggregation is a `VIEW ENTITY`** (OQL, Mendix 10.18+) — not a microflow that
  retrieves rows and counts them. The database does the work instead of pulling every
  object into memory. `mxcli syntax view-entity`, skill `write-oql-queries`.
- **A `/** ... */` comment before a statement sets that element's documentation.**
- **`@Position(x, y)` is optional** — mxcli places microflow activities, and
  `./mxcli layout` arranges the domain model.

## Finishing a change

Bootstrap set these up; they are only worth having if every change keeps them.

1. **Run the gates above, in order**, and say what each reported — not "it builds".
2. **Capture requirements as they arrive** — `./mxcli brain capture "<requirement>"
   --slice <slice> -a @Mod.Thing`. Never tick anything off: `brain plan` derives what
   is built from the model, so finishing the work is what moves the number.
3. **Append to `FINDINGS.md`** — anything surprising or broken, and how you verified it.
4. **Commit.** An idle session is reaped and its container goes with it; whatever is
   uncommitted is gone, including the model.

## Start here (all AI agents, every session)

1. **Read `docs/progress/RESUME.md` first, and nothing else yet.** Where we are, the next
   actions, and a table saying which larger file to open for the task at hand. Do NOT read
   `PROJECT.md` to get oriented — it is a decision register, not a resume doc.
   If that file is not there: `bin/init-project.sh` scaffolds it and `bin/close-task.sh`
   overwrites it at the end of each session, so its absence means neither has run here. Get
   oriented from `CLAUDE.local.md` (wiring + baseline routing) and `intake.md` instead, and
   say in chat that you did — never from `PROJECT.md`.
2. **`CLAUDE.md` is the canonical project instruction file** regardless of which agent you
   are. Every other instruction file in this repo, including this one, is a pointer to it.
3. **Exec approval defaults to `auto` (2026-09-16).** State the resolved mode once, at session
   start: "Exec approval: auto — I run scripts through bin/exec.sh and log them; say 'ask before
   exec' to switch." Before any `./mxcli exec`, `./bin/exec.sh`, `mxcli test`, `mxcli docker
   check`, or any `--mcp` write against the real `.mpr` — all of those mutate the model, the
   last two despite sounding read-only — check `/root/Mendix/mxcli-project-toolkit/bin/exec-approval.sh <project-root>`. Under
   `auto`, run it without asking and say in chat what ran; under `ask`, ask first, every time.
   The user switches either way by saying so — only then run
   `bin/exec-approval.sh <project-root> --set auto` / `--set ask`, never on your own judgement.
   Even on `auto`, SAY in chat (don't ask) before a STOP-table operation — drops on entities
   with data, `ALTER SETTINGS`, security level changes, cross-module moves — see
   `skills/learned-mdl-preflight.md`'s STOP table.
4. **`./mxcli`, not `mxcli`.** The binary is in the project root, never on PATH.
5. **Every model write goes through `./bin/exec.sh <script.mdl>` — never a bare `mxcli exec`.**
   exec.sh is the only thing that runs the mxbuild gate (`mxcli check` cannot see a consistency
   error such as CE0117), and it refuses to write when that gate cannot run. A bare exec leaves
   no gate row and no verification stamp, and the pre-commit hook then refuses the model until
   `./bin/verify-model.sh` has passed it.
6. **No new `.md`/`.html` in the project root.** Use docs/ architecture/ analysis/ design/.
   `bin/check-root-clean.sh` fails the build on strays.

Skill guides live in `.ai-context/skills/` — read the relevant one before writing MDL.
